record.summary: Declaration by 28 countries and the EU on the risks of 'frontier' AI: highly capable general-purpose models, and narrow AI with harmful capabilities, that match or exceed today's most advanced models. It warns of substantial risks from intentional misuse or unintended issues of control, names cybersecurity, biotechnology and disinformation, and sees potential for serious, even catastrophic, harm. Its agenda is a shared scientific understanding of these risks and risk-based national policies, with safety testing, evaluations and transparency from developers of frontier AI, and an international network of scientific research on frontier AI safety.
record.notes: Agreed at the AI Safety Summit at Bletchley Park, 1-2 November 2023; the countries represented include the US, China and the EU. New Zealand joined the commitment on 23 October 2024, and GOV.UK updated the publication on 13 February 2025 to include it as a signatory. The participants said they would meet again in 2024. The International AI Safety Report (interim report INT-08, full report INT-09) was launched at this summit. GOV.UK also offers a Latin American Spanish version of the publication.

verification.note: Stored and read: the declaration's HTML text on GOV.UK (official, stored 11 Oct 2026 and unchanged on 17 Oct 2026), which confirms the title, the text, the 28 countries and the EU represented and New Zealand's accession of 23 October 2024; and, in this run, the GOV.UK publication page (proposed as secondary_url), which gives the first publication on 1 November 2023 and the update of 13 February 2025 that added New Zealand, and DSIT's press release of 29 January 2025, which says the International AI Safety Report was launched at the summit. Version 1's claim that the text was unchanged by the 2025 update, and its description as the 'first' declaration of its kind, are not supported and were removed.

legal_force.quote: we resolve to support an internationally inclusive network of scientific research on frontier AI safety
We encourage all relevant actors to provide context-appropriate transparency and accountability

summary.quote: Particular safety risks arise at the 'frontier' of AI, understood as being those highly capable general-purpose AI models, including foundation models, that could perform a wide variety of tasks
Substantial risks may arise from potential intentional misuse or unintended issues of control relating to alignment with human intent.
We are especially concerned by such risks in domains such as cybersecurity and biotechnology, as well as where frontier AI systems may amplify risks such as disinformation.
There is potential for serious, even catastrophic, harm, either deliberate or unintentional
alongside increased transparency by private actors developing frontier AI capabilities, appropriate evaluation metrics, tools for safety testing
including through systems for safety testing, through evaluations, and by other appropriate measures

notes.quote: On 23 October 2024, New Zealand joined the commitment to the Bletchley Declaration.
